Individual Awards & Honors
Research Area — Player and coach honors beyond team titles
Headlined by Jaden Bradley's Gatorade POY and Reigan Richardson's McDonald's All-American honor; the CISAA POY
streak shows sustained boys-basketball talent.
AT A GLANCE
Gatorade POY Jaden Bradley — 2020 NC Gatorade Player of the Year (boys basketball)
AND MaxPreps national honoree, as a Cannon sophomore.
McDonald's Reigan Richardson ('21) — McDonald's All-American and Charlotte
All-American Observer State POY at Cannon, now a Duke star.
CISAA POY streak Four CONSECUTIVE Cannon boys-basketball players have won CISAA
Player of the Year (most recently Austin Swartz, unanimous).
Golf POY A 2014 girls' golf state champion was also named Charlotte Observer
Player of the Year.
AD recognition Athletic Director Chris Satterfield holds multiple NCADA and CMS Athletic
Director Awards.
Gatorade & National Player-of-the-Year Honors
Cannon's marquee individual honor is Jaden Bradley's 2020 North Carolina Gatorade Player of the Year
award in boys basketball — earned as a Cannon sophomore, when he averaged 23.1 points, 6.4 rebounds,
6.1 assists, and 2.9 steals, led the Cougars to a state title, and also drew MaxPreps national recognition and
conference Player of the Year honors. [Sources: NBA.com; Wikipedia — Jaden Bradley]
McDonald's All-American
Reigan Richardson (Class of 2021) was a 2021 McDonald's All-American, the 2020 Charlotte Observer
State of North Carolina Player of the Year, a CISAA Player of the Year, and NCISAA First-Team All-State —
ranked the No. 34 overall recruit nationally (No. 14 guard) by espnW before starring at Duke. [Sources:
Duke athletics/espnW; Charlotte Observer]
CISAA Players of the Year (Boys Basketball)
Cannon's most distinctive individual-honor story is its dominance of the CISAA Player of the Year award in
boys basketball: four consecutive winners, capped by Austin Swartz's unanimous selection. [Source:
Cannon Men's Basketball]
• Austin Swartz — unanimous CISAA Player of the Year (most recent); fourth straight Cannon
boys-basketball winner.
• Isaiah Henry — CISAA All-Conference selection.
• (The three earlier consecutive CISAA POY winners are referenced by the program but were not individually
named in this pass.)

CANNON SCHOOL COUGARS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Concord, NC
Coaches, Pedigree & Continuity
Research Area — Leadership, coaching backgrounds, and program stability
Long-tenured AD (Satterfield) and S&C; director (Powell); alumnus-led girls dynasty (Drakeford); a newly hired
Division-I-parent volleyball coach (Rosser).
AT A GLANCE
Athletic Director Chris Satterfield — 15+ years' leadership; multiple NCADA & CMS Athletic
Director Awards.
Girls Basketball Kelvin Drakeford — Cannon alum (played at Catawba College); 11th
season at Cannon, led the dynasty.
Sports Performance Shawn Powell — Director of Sports Performance / Head S&C; since 2014;
grade-by-grade development philosophy.
New hire Volleyball's Geoff Rosser — a Division I parent (daughter played at
Georgia Southern), hired to build a championship culture.
Continuity signal Long-tenured AD and S&C; director; an alumnus leading the flagship girls
program.
Athletic Department Leadership
Name Role & Background
Chris Satterfield Director of Athletics — 15+ yrs; multiple NCADA & CMS AD Awards.
Kevin Steuer Associate AD (joined 2022) — previously AD at The Williams School (CT), Asst AD at
Thayer Academy, SID at Buckingham, Browne & Nichols.
Holly Pente Assistant AD (since 2024) — Cannon's Head Athletic Trainer 2013–2024; ECU
athletic-training degree; previously with Novant Health.
Craig Reynolds Athletics media/communications (longtime Cannon parent & volunteer).
[Source: Cannon School Athletics staff pages]
Girls Basketball — Kelvin Drakeford (continuity anchor)
Drakeford embodies Cannon's continuity story. A Cannon School alumnus who competed for the Cougars
and went on to play at Catawba College, he is in his 11th season at the school and 6th as Program Director,
having previously spent five seasons as the boys' JV head coach and varsity assistant. He led the girls
program to its first-ever state championship and the dynasty that followed, describing that first title as his
favorite Cannon memory. His stated coaching values: “giving players confidence, leading with love, teaching
with purpose, expecting greatness, and turning failure into growth.” The culture he built helped attract elite
talent — future McDonald's All-American Reigan Richardson transferred in from public Hickory Ridge and
led the 2021 title run, and Drakeford has continued to draw high-major recruits such as Jakaila Gaskin.
[Sources: Cannon School girls basketball team page; Charlotte Observer]
Strength & Conditioning — Shawn Powell
Compiled June 17, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
CANNON SCHOOL COUGARS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Concord, NC
Shawn Powell has been Cannon's Head Strength & Conditioning Coach / Director of Sports Performance
since May 2014 (after five years as a head S&C; coach elsewhere), giving the performance program a
decade of continuity. His philosophy opens with 7th graders by asking “What's your purpose for being here?”
and runs a vertically aligned, grade-by-grade “block” system (detailed in the Sports Medicine & Performance
document). He is supported by S&C; coach Duncan Hundley (Liberty University, bachelor's in physical
education; Clemson, master's in athletic leadership). [Sources: Cannon Athletics “Fit for Life”; staff pages]
Other Coaches
• Volleyball — Geoff Rosser (newly hired): previously on staff at Cox Mill HS (two state championship finals)
and led Mountain Island Charter to a conference title; a Division I parent (daughter Robin played at
Georgia Southern), bringing a recruiting-process perspective. Cannon AD Chris Satterfield called him
“uniquely qualified to lead our program.”
• Boys Basketball — a CISAA-contending program (state titles 2006/2020/2021; four straight CISAA
Players of the Year); the current head coach's name was not confirmed in this pass.
• [Sources: Cannon School News; Cannon Men's Basketball]
Continuity & Stability — Summary
• A long-tenured athletic director (Satterfield, 15+ years) and S&C; director (Powell, since 2014) provide
departmental stability.
• An alumnus (Drakeford) leads the flagship girls basketball dynasty — a strong homegrown-continuity story.
• An integrated model: athletic training (Novant partnership) and strength & conditioning explicitly “operate
as one team,” per Powell.
• Targeted external hiring for program upgrades (e.g., Rosser in volleyball) paired with internal promotion
(Pente from Head AT to Assistant AD).
Notes & Gaps
• Several head-coach names (boys basketball, football, and most non-flagship sports) were not confirmed in
this pass; Cannon's per-team pages are the follow-up.
• Exact tenures beyond Satterfield, Powell, and Drakeford are not all published.

Athletic Facilities & Infrastructure
Research Area — Grounds by sport, buildings, and the Campus Master Plan
Sourced from Cannon's Campus History and current capital campaign (explicitly tied to the Campus Master Plan): grounds
by sport, the Randy Marion Field House, Andrews Strength Center, and Hill Grimmett Center.
AT A GLANCE
Campus 65-acre campus at 5801 Poplar Tent Road, Concord, NC.
Capital history The “Building Bright Futures” campaign built the Andrews Strength &
Conditioning Center, Randy Marion Family Field House, and an expanded
Middle School.

Campus & Capital History
Cannon School sits on a 65-acre campus at 5801 Poplar Tent Road in Concord, NC, one mile east of I-85.
The school's published “Our Campus & History” timeline functions as a master-plan record, and a current
capital campaign (“A Flourishing Future”) explicitly describes its Upper School project as “a key initiative
within our Campus Master Plan.” [Sources: Cannon School — Our Campus & History; A Flourishing Future
capital campaign]
Outdoor Grounds by Sport
Sport Grounds / Venue
Football / Soccer / The newly configured track and field, modernized as part of a major Upper School
Lacrosse / Track expansion; accommodates track & field, soccer, lacrosse, and football. The Randy Marion
Field added an all-weather artificial-turf surface for play in any conditions.
Baseball On-campus baseball field with a batting facility (specific name not confirmed in this pass).
Softball A dedicated on-campus softball field.
Tennis On-campus tennis courts (count not confirmed in this pass).
Golf No dedicated on-campus course; the program practices/competes at an outside club (not
confirmed by name).

and meet venue was not confirmed — see Notes & Gaps.

Indoor & Support Buildings
• Randy Marion Family Field House — built as part of the “Building Bright Futures” campaign; includes a
press box with three booths (calling, video, scoring) and was a leadership gift from Betty & Randy Marion
Sr. in honor of their grandchildren.
• Andrews Strength & Conditioning Center — two floors; built in the same capital campaign; described as
rivaling any college facility (full equipment detail below).
• Hill Grimmett Multipurpose Athletic Center — 5,000 sq ft flex space used for wrestling, MS recess,
cheer practice, batting cages and pitching areas, and speed & agility training.
• Boswell Gym — the main competition gym for basketball, with its court named (Jan 2019) for longtime
announcers Mike Hoffman and the late John Riley; plus an adjacent Auxiliary Gym.
• Enhanced locker spaces and coaches' offices — also delivered as part of the “Building Bright Futures”
campaign.
• [Sources: Cannon School — Our Campus & History; Cannon Athletics Facilities page]
Strength & Conditioning — Equipment Detail
• First floor (8 fully-equipped strength stations): nine Legend Fitness racks and four Dynamic Fitness &
Strength racks with benches; 90-lb PowerBlock dumbbells; medicine balls and bands; sixteen 45-lb lifting
bars and four 25-lb bars; eight kettlebell handles; plyo boxes; ten Jungle Gym XT suspension trainers.
• Second floor: four spin cycles, two treadmills, and two rowing machines for rehabilitation, conditioning,
and low-impact cardio.
• Access: open to ALL Cannon students during the school year, plus a free summer training program.
• [Source: Cannon Athletics Strength & Conditioning / Facilities pages]
What's Underway: A Flourishing Future
Cannon's current capital campaign, “A Flourishing Future,” is funding a 12,500-sq-ft expansion and
renovation of the Upper School (flexible classrooms, modern science labs, open student spaces) along with
new Academic Resource Centers across divisions. The project's official groundbreaking took place in June;
the school expects renovations to be complete by the start of the 2026–27 school year. While this campaign
is primarily academic, the school explicitly frames it as part of the broader Campus Master Plan that has
historically included athletics facilities. [Source: Cannon School — A Flourishing Future]
Game-Day & Broadcast Infrastructure
• Live streaming and highlights via Hudl (fan.hudl.com).
• A dedicated athletics media/communications lead (Craig Reynolds) producing media days and managing
social platforms; a Cannon Athletics Boosters (CAB) organization that also powers the Cannon Athletics
Leadership Academy.
• A press box with three booths in the Randy Marion Family Field House.
• [Source: Cannon Athletics site map / facilities pages; Hudl]

Compiled June 17, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 2

• No on-campus swimming pool/natatorium was identified for Cannon in this pass; the swim team's home

• Golf's home course/practice facility and the baseball field's specific name were not identified.
• Seating capacities for the stadium and Boswell Gym were not published in the sources reviewed.
• The exact square footage of the Randy Marion Family Field House and the Andrews Strength Center are
cited at slightly different figures across Cannon's own pages (4,800 vs. 4,100 sq ft in earlier research);
confirm exact numbers directly with the school before stating precisely on-air.

AT A GLANCE

public schools were banned.

The NCISAA NIL Policy (Applies to Cannon)
In February 2024, the North Carolina Independent Schools Athletic Association — which governs roughly
94–100 private schools including Cannon — approved a policy allowing its student-athletes to profit from
their name, image, and likeness while retaining eligibility, effective the 2024–25 school year. [Sources:
HighSchoolOT; On3]
Key rules:
• NIL activity must be kept SEPARATE from interscholastic participation; athletes may not use the school's
name/marks or appear in uniform in NIL deals.
• Prohibited categories include cannabis, alcohol, gambling, adult entertainment, drugs, and tobacco.
• All NIL agreements must be reported to and approved by the NCISAA state office.
• School personnel may not use NIL to recruit/enroll students or act as an athlete's agent.
• Violations can trigger a suspension (reported as up to 60 days).
• [Sources: On3; Lewis Brisbois sports-law analysis]
The Contrast: NC Public Schools
Public-school NIL took the opposite path: the NCHSAA approved a policy in 2023, the legislature intervened
(SB 636), the State Board of Education banned public-school NIL in June 2024, and it only became
permanently legal on July 1, 2025 (Brandon v. State Board of Education; SB 563, which created an NC NIL
Clearinghouse and a 50% business tax credit). For about a year, NCISAA schools like Cannon had an NIL
window their public-school counterparts did not. [Sources: HighSchoolOT; RallyFuel NC NIL guide]

Cannon is well-placed to benefit from NIL in the same structural way other NCISAA schools are — and
arguably most in basketball, where its girls dynasty and boys CISAA-Player-of-the-Year pipeline create

biggest games — live in its basketball programs. [Source: MaxPreps]

CANNON SCHOOL COUGARS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Concord, NC
Sports Medicine, Athletic Training &
Strength/Conditioning
Research Area — On-site care, the Novant Health partnership, and year-round
performance
A real regional-health-system partnership: Novant Health provides full-time certified athletic trainers, plus two named team
physicians.
AT A GLANCE
Health-system partner Novant Health — provides full-time certified athletic trainers.
Team physicians Dr. Bryan Edwards and Dr. Jess Kirby — both Novant Health Presbyterian
orthopedic surgeons.
Athletic trainers Holly Pente (Head AT 2013–2024, now Asst AD) and Hayley Goldman
(Certified AT with Novant).
Sports performance Director Shawn Powell (since 2014) runs a grade-by-grade “block”
development system; integrated with athletic training.
Academic tie Cannon is a clinical site for UNC Charlotte's Master's in Athletic Training
program.
The Novant Health Partnership
Cannon has a genuine regional-healthcare-giant partnership, real and stated: “Through a valued partnership
with Novant Health, Cannon School benefits from the full-time support of certified athletic trainers who
provide reliable, high-quality care to our student-athletes every day.” Cannon's sports-medicine model is
proactive and on-site, with trainers present at every venue as the first medical professionals on scene after
an injury, collaborating with team physicians on emergency and follow-up care. [Source: Cannon Athletics
— Athletic Training page]
Team Physicians
Physician Background
Dr. Bryan Edwards, MD Orthopedic surgeon, Cornelius NC; affiliated with Novant Health Presbyterian Medical
Center. Wake Forest University grad; MD from Brody School of Medicine (ECU);
residency at Medical College of Georgia; sports-medicine fellowship with the Atlanta
Falcons.
Dr. Jess Kirby, MD Orthopedic surgeon, Cornelius NC; affiliated with Novant Health Presbyterian Medical
Center. Texas A&M; University grad; MD from University of Texas Medical Branch.
[Source: Cannon Athletics — Athletic Training page]
Athletic Training Staff & Model
• Holly Pente — Cannon's Head Athletic Trainer from June 2013 to May 2024, now Assistant Athletic
Director; ECU athletic-training degree; previously employed by Novant Health.
Compiled June 17, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
CANNON SCHOOL COUGARS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Concord, NC
• Hayley Goldman — Certified Athletic Trainer with Novant Health; UNC Charlotte athletic-training degree;
previously in the Union County high-school setting.
• Return-to-Play (RTP) coordinator — oversees a structured return protocol requiring functional testing
and, when appropriate, physician clearance before an athlete resumes competition.
• Clinical education site — Cannon hosts UNC Charlotte Master's in Athletic Training students, with its
trainers serving as mentors/supervisors.
• [Source: Cannon Athletics — Athletic Training page; Cannon Athletics staff pages]
Strength & Conditioning — Philosophy and System
Cannon's Director of Sports Performance, Shawn Powell (head S&C; since May 2014), runs a program built
on intention — he opens with 7th graders by asking, “What's your purpose for being here?” The program is
vertically aligned through a grade-by-grade “block” system, and the strength and athletic-training
departments explicitly “operate as one team” in a high-performance model. [Source: Cannon Athletics — “Fit
for Life”]
• Block 0 (7th–8th grade): body control, balance, basic strength.
• Block 1 (9th grade): leadership and teamwork through foundational lifts.
• Block 2 (10th grade): building consistent strength.
• Block 3 (11th–12th grade): advanced training, data application, and recovery strategies.
• Staff & partners: S&C; coach Duncan Hundley (Liberty University, B.S. physical education; Clemson,
M.S. athletic leadership); an internship partnership with UNC Charlotte's Exercise Science Department.
• Reach: open to all students, not just varsity.
• [Source: Cannon Athletics — “Fit for Life”; Strength & Conditioning page]
Notes & Gaps
• The current Head Athletic Trainer's name (post-2024, after Holly Pente moved to Assistant AD) was not
confirmed in this pass; Hayley Goldman is a confirmed current certified AT.
• The total number of full-time ATs under the Novant partnership was not stated precisely.

Overview
Cannon School is an independent, co-educational, junior-kindergarten-through-12th-grade
college-preparatory school in Concord, North Carolina, just northeast of Charlotte. Its athletics program
competes in the NCISAA for state championships and in the CISAA for conference play. The program is
organized around three stated pillars: “Leading with Purpose, Building Together, and Growing Relentlessly.”
[Sources: Cannon School Athletics (athletics.cannonschool.org); MaxPreps Cannon Cougars page]
Complete List of Sports
Cannon sponsors 13 distinct sports. Counting boys' and girls' programs separately, as below, yields 21
varsity programs. Each is offered at the varsity level; most also field JV and Middle School (often split into
“Maroon” and “Gold”) teams. [Sources: MaxPreps Cannon Cougars sport index; cannonschool.org Team
Pages]

Beyond the teams themselves, Cannon runs a distinctive leadership program, the Cannon Athletics

accepted more than 90 student-athletes (classes of 2027–2030) into its first full-year cohort for 2026–27.

• Boys Basketball — a Charlotte-area power with NCISAA state titles (2006, 2020, 2021) and four
consecutive CISAA Players of the Year. [Source: Cannon Men's Basketball]

reached professional golf tours. [Source: Cannon Athletics Hall of Fame]

[Source: Cannon Athletics Hall of Fame]

Team Win-Loss Records — Recent Seasons
Research Area — Top 5 sports, both genders where applicable
Covers Cannon's top 5 sports: Girls Basketball, Boys Basketball, Football, Golf (B&G;), and Cross Country/Track (B&G;).
AT A GLANCE
Top 5 sports Girls Basketball, Boys Basketball, Football, Golf (Boys & Girls), and Cross
Country/Track & Field (Boys & Girls) — selected by championship history
and recent prominence.
Girls Basketball Four NCISAA 4A titles in six years (2021, 2024–2026); routinely dominant
scores.
Boys Basketball 2025–26: beat two CISAA rivals (72–71, 87–71) before a state quarterfinal
exit.
Golf Both programs have won NCISAA state titles (boys 2015, girls 2014).
Cross Country Boys won Cannon's first-ever state title in any sport (2001).
How to Read This Document
Per the standard workflow, this document covers Cannon's top 5 sports by championship history and recent
prominence, with both boys' and girls' programs included wherever both exist and data is available. Records
were assembled from MaxPreps game logs, NCISAA brackets, the Cannon Athletics Hall of Fame, and
North Carolina sports media.
1. Girls Basketball — The Dynasty
• 2020–21: NCISAA 4A STATE CHAMPION — the program's first title, led by senior Reigan Richardson
(McDonald's All-American), 24 pts in the final vs North Raleigh Christian.
• 2023–24: NCISAA 4A STATE CHAMPION — 23 wins, 8–0 in CISAA play.
• 2024–25: NCISAA 4A STATE CHAMPION — defeated Wesleyan Christian Academy 71–55; in-season
wins of 75–10 (a CISAA rival), 80–52 (Forsyth Country Day), 55–45 (Rabun Gap).
• 2025–26: NCISAA 4A STATE CHAMPION — fourth title in six years; entered the season ranked No. 1 in
the Charlotte Observer Sweet 16.

under a coach who also built the Cannon Cross Country Invitational into a 20-year program fixture. Track &

the cross country course record, and was a 2016 800m State Champion before running at the University of
